# Merchant Financial Advisory LLC (MFA)

> Accounting, bookkeeping, tax preparation and advisory firm in Princeton, New Jersey. Serves small and mid-sized businesses and individuals in New Jersey, New York City and nationwide, forms LLCs in all 50 states, and sells digital tax and bookkeeping tools. Founded by Zain Merchant, ACCA, formerly of PwC.

Contact: info@mfa-advisory.com, (347) 205-4468. Location: Princeton, New Jersey (no public street address; work is done remotely by video, phone and secure upload). Languages: English, Hindi, Urdu. Book a 30-minute consultation: https://mfa-advisory.com/book/. Replies to inquiries within one business day.

Not a law firm. MFA does not perform audits or issue audit, review or compilation reports. Content on the site is general information, not tax, legal or financial advice.

## Tools (online calculators and checkers)
- [Resources hub](https://mfa-advisory.com/resources/): all tools, calendars, templates and guides
- [1099 Contractor Tracker: Who Needs a 1099-NEC in 2026](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/1099-contractor-tracker/): Track vendors, W-9s and payments, see who needs a 1099-NEC at the 2026 $2,000 threshold, and export to CSV. Data stays in your browser.
- [1099 Tax Calculator 2026: Self-Employment, NJ & NY](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/1099-tax-calculator/): Estimate the self-employment tax, federal income tax and NJ or NY tax on your 1099 income, plus the share of every payment to set aside.
- [Break-Even Calculator for Small Businesses](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/break-even-calculator/): Find your break-even point in sales and units from monthly fixed costs, price and variable cost. For product and service businesses, with a profit goal.
- [Do I Need to Send a 1099? 2026 Payments Checker](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/do-i-need-to-send-a-1099/): Four questions show whether a 2026 payment needs a Form 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC: the $2,000 threshold, card and corporation exceptions, and deadlines.
- [Home Office Deduction Calculator 2026](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/home-office-deduction-calculator/): Compare the simplified ($5 per square foot, up to 300) and regular home office deduction methods for 2026 side by side.
- [Tax Write-Offs for Small Business: Is It Deductible?](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/): Tax write-offs for small business, 2026: search 59 everyday expenses for a plain answer, what proof to keep and the mistake to avoid.
- [Mileage Deduction Calculator 2026 (IRS Standard Rates)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/mileage-deduction-calculator/): Calculate your 2026 business mileage deduction with the IRS standard rates, including the split between the January to June and July to December rates.
- [Paycheck Tax Calculator 2026 (Federal, FICA, NJ & NY)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/paycheck-tax-calculator/): Estimate W-2 take-home pay per paycheck after federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare and New Jersey or New York tax.
- [Profit Margin & Markup Calculator](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/): Calculate gross profit margin and markup from cost and price, or the selling price for a target margin or markup. Includes a margin vs. markup guide.
- [Quarterly Estimated Tax Calculator 2026: Fed, NJ & NY](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/quarterly-estimated-tax-calculator/): Estimate your four 2026 quarterly tax payments: self-employment tax, federal income tax and NJ or NY tax, with due dates and the penalty-safe amount.
- [S Corp Tax Savings Calculator: Is an S Corp Worth It?](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/s-corp-tax-savings-calculator/): Compare self-employment tax as an LLC with payroll taxes as an S corporation. See annual savings after costs and the break-even profit.
- [2027 Business Tax Deadlines by Entity: Fed, NJ & NY](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/tax-deadlines-2027/): Every 2027 federal, New Jersey and New York tax deadline for sole proprietors, partnerships, S and C corporations, employers and nonprofits.
- [W-9 Request Email Templates for Vendors](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/w-9-request-email-template/): Copy-ready W-9 request emails for new vendors, year-end 1099 prep and reminders. Personalize the names and deadline, then copy with one click.

## Is It Deductible? (2026 business expense deductions, one line per expense)
- [Is it tax deductible? 2026 business write-off finder](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/): search 59 common business expenses; verdict, rule, limits, records to keep and the IRS source for each
- [Dataset (JSON)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/deductions.json): the same entries as structured data. Cite with a link to the page.
- [Home office](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#home-office): Partly. If a specific spot in your home is used only and regularly for your business, and it's your main place of work (or where you meet clients), part of your home costs counts. The easy way: $5 per square foot, up to 300 square feet.
- [Office rent](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#office-rent): Yes. Rent for an office, shop, studio or storefront you use for your business counts in full.
- [Coworking space or shared desk](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#coworking): Yes. A coworking membership, desk rental or meeting room you book for work counts as rent for business space. If the membership bundles in personal perks like a gym, only the business part counts.
- [Utilities (electric, gas, water)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#utilities): Partly. For a shop, office or studio, yes. For your home, only through the home office deduction: the work-space share of the bills counts if you use the regular method.
- [Office supplies and postage](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#office-supplies): Yes. Paper, ink, pens, stamps and other supplies you use up in your business count. Things that last well over a year are treated as equipment instead.
- [Work clothes and uniforms](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#uniforms): Usually not. Only if your work requires it and it isn't something you could wear as everyday clothing, like protective gear, scrubs or a uniform you wouldn't wear outside work. Regular clothes don't count, even if you only wear them for work.
- [Car mileage (standard rate)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#mileage): Partly. Yes for business driving, never for your commute. The easy way: multiply your business miles by the IRS rate, 72.5 cents a mile for January to June 2026 and 76 cents from July to December. Business parking and tolls count on top.
- [Car expenses (actual costs)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#vehicle-actual-expenses): Partly. Instead of the mileage rate, you can write off the work share of what your car really costs: gas, repairs, tires, insurance, registration, and depreciation or lease payments. If 70% of your miles are for work, 70% of those costs count.
- [Parking and tolls](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#parking-tolls): Yes. Parking and tolls on business trips count, on top of mileage or actual car costs. Parking at your own regular workplace doesn't, because that's commuting.
- [Business travel (flights, hotels)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-travel): Yes. Yes, when work takes you away from home overnight: flights, hotels, rides and taxis there, baggage and laundry. Meals on the trip count at half. A trip that's mainly a vacation doesn't count.
- [Meals while traveling](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#travel-meals): Partly. Meals while you're away overnight on business count at 50%. Keep your receipts, or use the IRS daily meal allowance for the area instead.
- [Business meals](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#meals): Partly. A meal with a client, customer or business contact counts at 50%, tax and tip included, as long as you're there, it isn't over the top, and there's a real business reason.
- [Entertainment (tickets, golf, shows)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#entertainment): Usually not. Game tickets, golf, concerts and shows don't count, even with a client and a real business reason. Food bought separately at the event can still count as a half-off business meal.
- [Staff parties and team events](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-parties): Yes. Yes, in full. A holiday party or summer picnic mainly for your team counts 100%, not just half, as long as it's for your staff in general and not only your top earners.
- [Snacks and meals for employees at work](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-meals): Usually not. No, starting in 2026. Snacks, coffee and meals you provide to employees at work are no longer deductible, apart from a few narrow exceptions. Staff parties follow a different rule.
- [Cell phone and phone service](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#cell-phone): Partly. The work share of your phone bill counts. If you use your phone 60% for work, you can write off 60% of the bill. The phone itself is equipment and is written off separately.
- [Internet service](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#internet): Partly. At a business location, all of it counts. At home, only the work share does.
- [Software and subscriptions](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#software-subscriptions): Yes. Monthly or yearly subscriptions you use for your business, like QuickBooks, Canva, Zoom or Adobe, count. If you also use one personally, only the business share counts.
- [Laptop or computer](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#computer): Yes. Usually yes, for the share you use for work. You can often write off a work laptop all at once (for example, if it costs $2,500 or less), or spread it over a few years.
- [Equipment and machinery (Section 179)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#section-179): Yes. Furniture, machines and other equipment for your business can usually be written off in full the year you start using it, instead of over several years. The write-off can't be more than your business income; any extra moves to next year.
- [Bonus depreciation](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#bonus-depreciation): Yes. Most business equipment bought after Jan. 19, 2025 can be written off 100% in the first year. You can also choose to spread it out instead.
- [Small equipment purchases ($2,500 or less)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#de-minimis-safe-harbor): Yes. Items that cost $2,500 or less each (or per invoice) can be written off right away instead of over several years, if you choose this rule each year on your tax return.
- [Tools and small equipment](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#tools-equipment): Yes. Tools you use up within a year count when you buy them. Bigger, longer-lasting tools are spread over a few years, though many can be written off right away under the small-purchase or equipment rules. If you also use them personally, only the work share counts.
- [Repairs vs. improvements](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#repairs-vs-improvements): Yes. Fixing something to keep it working counts right away. Making it better, bigger or fit for a new use is an improvement, written off over several years. Smaller businesses may be able to write off repairs and improvements on a building right away, up to the lesser of $10,000 or 2% of the building's cost.
- [Contractor and freelancer payments](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#contractors): Yes. What you pay freelancers and contractors for work on your business counts in full. If you pay someone $2,000 or more for services in 2026, you'll usually need to send them a 1099-NEC.
- [Employee wages](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#wages): Yes. Reasonable pay, salaries and bonuses for your employees count. What you take out for yourself as a sole owner (owner's draws) doesn't.
- [Employer payroll taxes](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#payroll-taxes): Yes. Your share as the employer of Social Security, Medicare and unemployment taxes counts. The taxes you hold back from employees' paychecks are part of their pay, not an extra write-off.
- [Employee benefit programs](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-benefits): Yes. What you pay toward your employees' health plans, group life insurance and dependent care help counts. Your own benefits as a self-employed owner don't go here.
- [Employee awards and holiday gifts](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#achievement-awards): Yes. Yes, within limits. Awards for years of service or safety (real items, not cash) count up to $400 per employee a year. Small, low-value holiday gifts count too. Cash and gift cards are treated as wages.
- [Business insurance](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-insurance): Yes. Insurance for your business, like general or professional liability, property or workers' comp coverage, counts in full. Health insurance follows its own rules.
- [Health insurance (self-employed)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#self-employed-health-insurance): Yes. Usually yes, if you're self-employed and your business made a profit. Health, dental, vision and qualified long-term care premiums for you and your family count, on your personal return. Not for any month you or your spouse could have joined an employer's subsidized plan.
- [Life insurance premiums](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#life-insurance): Usually not. Life insurance on yourself is personal, and you can't write off premiums when you or your business would get the payout. Group life coverage for employees can count as a benefit.
- [SEP-IRA contributions](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#sep-ira): Yes. Money you put into a SEP-IRA for yourself lowers your taxes, on your personal return. For 2026 the cap is 25% of pay or $72,000, whichever is less, and for the self-employed the math works out a bit lower. You can open and fund it up to your tax deadline, including extensions.
- [Solo 401(k) contributions](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#solo-401k): Yes. If it's just you, a solo 401(k) lets you save as both the "employee" and the "employer." For 2026: up to $24,500 as the employee, plus extra if you're 50 or older, and up to $72,000 in total. You claim it on your personal return.
- [Retirement contributions for employees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-retirement): Yes. Matches and other contributions you make to your employees' retirement plans count as a business expense.
- [Legal and accounting fees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#legal-professional-fees): Yes. Fees for accountants, bookkeepers, lawyers and other pros you hire for your business count in full. Personal legal fees, like a will or a divorce, don't.
- [Tax preparation fees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#tax-prep-fees): Partly. The cost of preparing the business part of your return counts. The part for the rest of your personal return doesn't, so ask your preparer to split the bill.
- [Professional and trade association dues](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#professional-dues): Yes. Dues for professional groups, trade associations and the chamber of commerce count. Social clubs, golf clubs and gyms never do.
- [Advertising and marketing](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#advertising): Yes. Ads, business cards, flyers, Google or Instagram ads and other marketing count in full.
- [Gifts to clients](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#client-gifts): Partly. Up to $25 per person per year. Wrapping, engraving and shipping don't count toward the $25.
- [Branded promotional items](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#promotional-items): Yes. Low-cost items with your logo that you hand out widely, like pens or keychains, aren't treated as gifts, so the $25 limit doesn't apply. They need to cost $4 or less each.
- [Courses, training and conferences](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-education): Yes. Yes, if it keeps up or improves skills for the work you already do. Not if it trains you for a new line of work, or covers the basic requirements to get into your field.
- [Bank and card processing fees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#bank-card-fees): Yes. Fees on your business bank account, wire fees and the cut Stripe, Square or PayPal takes from your sales all count.
- [Interest on business loans and credit cards](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-interest): Partly. Interest on money borrowed for your business counts. On a card or loan used for both business and personal spending, only the business share counts.
- [Unpaid invoices (bad debts)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#bad-debts): Usually not. Usually not for small businesses. If you never counted the unpaid invoice as income (most small businesses don't until they're paid), there's nothing to write off.
- [Startup costs](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#startup-costs): Partly. Costs before you open, like market research, pre-launch ads or training, can be written off up to $5,000 in your first year. The rest is spread over 15 years.
- [Business formation costs](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#organizational-costs): Partly. Costs to form a partnership or corporation (including a multi-member LLC), like state filing and legal fees, can be written off up to $5,000 in the first year, with the rest spread over 15 years.
- [Inventory and cost of goods sold](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#inventory-cogs): Yes. Products you buy or make to sell count when they sell, not when you buy them. Smaller businesses can often use a simpler method.
- [Shipping and postage](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#shipping-postage): Yes. Shipping orders to customers and business postage count in full.
- [Self-employment tax](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#self-employment-tax): Partly. You can write off half of your self-employment tax on your personal return. It lowers your income tax, not the self-employment tax itself.
- [Business taxes](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-taxes): Partly. Property taxes on business assets and some business taxes count. Federal income tax and self-employment tax never do, and sales tax you collect from customers and pass on isn't yours to write off.
- [Business licenses and permits](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#licenses-permits): Yes. Yearly business licenses, permits and state or local regulatory fees count.
- [Commuting](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#commuting): Usually not. Getting from home to your regular workplace is personal, however far it is. But if your home office is your main place of business, trips from there to clients or job sites can count.
- [Fines and penalties](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#fines-penalties): Usually not. Parking tickets, speeding tickets and IRS penalties can't be written off, even if you got them while working.
- [Political contributions and lobbying](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#political-lobbying): Usually not. Donations to candidates, campaigns and political parties, and most lobbying costs, can't be written off.
- [Club memberships](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#club-dues): Usually not. Country clubs, golf clubs, gyms and other social or athletic clubs don't count, even if you meet clients there. Professional groups and the chamber of commerce are different.
- [Gym and fitness memberships](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#gym): Usually not. Gym, health club and fitness memberships are personal, even if staying fit helps you work. Meeting clients there doesn't change that.
- [Personal expenses](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#personal-expenses): Usually not. Groceries, your gym, haircuts, vacations and family costs aren't business expenses, even if you pay with the business card. If something is used for both, only the business part counts.
- [Charitable donations by your business](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#charitable-contributions): Usually not. Not as a business expense if you're a sole owner. On your personal return they can count if you itemize, and starting in 2026 up to $1,000 in cash gifts ($2,000 for married couples filing jointly) counts even if you don't.
